findings.title: resourceStore.findByName uses client.getId() instead of client name consistently with getOrCreateResource
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, relying on the resource name being the client's ID. This matches AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource's resolveClient which stores the client's internal id as resource name, so it's consistent, but there's no safeguard/comment establishing that invariant; if resolveClient's resolution logic changes (e.g., returns clientId string instead of internal id) this lookup silently breaks, always returning false and denying all permissions, which is a hard-to-detect data integrity bug.

findings.title: hasPermission(String scope) does not fallback to resource-type resource consistently
findings.body: In hasPermission(String scope), `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` looks up the 'all clients' resource directly by name equal to the resource type constant ('Clients'), while hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) uses `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` to fetch it. These are two different code paths for retrieving the same conceptual resource; if the two diverge (e.g., schema changes resource naming logic), the all-clients scope checks in canManage()/canManageClientScopes() will silently stop working while per-client checks continue to work, causing inconsistent permission evaluation.

findings.title: Potential NPE if resource-type resource doesn't exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), if `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null (e.g., schema not initialized, or admin-permissions client never had init() run), the subsequent call `authz.getStoreFactore().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource may throw an NPE rather than gracefully returning false, causing an unhandled server error instead of a controlled permission denial.

findings.title: getScope performs unchecked map access for unsupported resourceType
findings.body: In getScope(), `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType)` is called without null-checking the result before calling `.getScopes()`. If resourceType is null or not present (e.g., CLIENTS newly introduced but caller passes mismatched/legacy type), this throws a NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException, resulting in an unclear 500 error for callers instead of a controlled 400.
